01.actor: A blind man who reviewed mishnayot before Mar Shmuel
01.event: The blind man was late one day; Mar Shmuel sent a messenger to his house, who missed him on the road and on returning reported that the blind man's wife had committed adultery.
01.turn: A lone witness accuses the wife, and the blind man must decide whether to act on it.
01.outcome: Mar Shmuel told him to divorce her if he trusted the messenger, and not to divorce her otherwise.
01.summary: A blind man used to review mishnayot before Mar Shmuel. One day he was late, so Mar Shmuel sent a messenger to fetch him; the two took different roads and missed each other. The messenger came back saying he had seen the man's wife committing adultery. The blind man asked Mar Shmuel what to do, and was told: if you trust this messenger, divorce her; if not, do not.

02.event: Sages asked Rabbi Yehoshua whether the rival wife of a daughter is exempt, and pressed him for whose view is the halakha.
02.turn: He refused to rule between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel, saying he feared they would break his skull.
02.outcome: Instead he testified that two great Jerusalem families descended from rival wives and produced High Priests.
02.summary: Sages asked Rabbi Yehoshua about the law of a daughter's rival wife. He said it was disputed between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel, and when pressed for the ruling he asked why they were putting his head between two great mountains, fearing they would crush his skull. Instead he offered testimony that two great Jerusalem families descended from such rival wives and produced High Priests.
02.missing: The exchange is mostly a halakhic question and answer; there is little event beyond the refusal and testimony.

03.actor: Rav Huna and his son Rabba
03.event: Rav Huna tore silk garments in front of his son Rabba to test whether he would become angry.
03.turn: The test of the son's restraint in honoring his father.
03.summary: Rav Huna wanted to see whether his son Rabba would honor him even under provocation, so he tore expensive silk garments in front of him. The Gemara discusses how this could be permitted, explaining that Rav Huna had forgone his honor in advance.
03.missing: The text does not say how Rabba reacted; the rest is legal discussion of the test.

04.actor: Mar Yehuda and the residents of Mavrakhta
04.event: Mar Yehuda found the residents of Mavrakhta placing their eiruv in the synagogue of Beit Agovar and told them to place it farther in to gain more distance.
04.turn: Rava rebuked him, calling him argumentative.
04.outcome: Rava declared that in eiruv matters no one follows Rabbi Akiva's opinion, so his advice was unnecessary.
04.summary: Mar Yehuda came upon the people of Mavrakhta depositing their eiruv in the Beit Agovar synagogue and advised them to put it deeper inside so their Shabbat limit would extend farther. Rava scolded him as quarrelsome, saying that in eiruv law nobody follows Rabbi Akiva's view on which his advice depended.

05.missing: This describes Rava's habitual practice when such cases came before him, not a single event.

06.actor: Ravina, in the presence of Rav Ashi
06.event: While sitting before Rav Ashi, Ravina saw a man tying his donkey to a palm tree on Shabbat, shouted at him, was ignored, and declared the man excommunicated.
06.turn: Ravina worried that he had acted irreverently by ruling in his teacher's presence.
06.outcome: Rav Ashi reassured him that where God's name is desecrated, no deference is owed even to a teacher.
06.summary: Ravina was sitting before his teacher Rav Ashi when he saw a man tie his donkey to a palm tree on Shabbat. Ravina shouted at him, but the man ignored him, so Ravina pronounced him excommunicated. Afterward he asked Rav Ashi whether this had been disrespectful to him, and Rav Ashi answered that where God's name is being desecrated, one does not defer to one's teacher.

07.event: Ravin went as an agent to betroth a woman for his son but betrothed her to himself.
07.turn: The woman's family would not give her to the son, and Ravin feared someone else would betroth her while he went to report back.
07.summary: Ravin the Pious set out to arrange a betrothal for his son, but ended up betrothing the woman to himself. The Gemara explains that her family refused to give her to the son, and that Ravin did not first tell his son because he feared that in the meantime someone else would betroth her.

08.missing: A case of betrothal with silk is cited only as the occasion for a legal dispute between Rabba and Rav Yosef; no narrative.

09.actor: Rav Yosef and his student Abaye
09.event: Rav Yosef, having forgotten his learning, said he had never heard a teaching, and Abaye reminded him that he himself had taught it to them.
09.turn: Rav Yosef recalled the teaching but in a different form than Abaye reported it.
09.outcome: Rav Yosef restated what he had actually taught, reconciling Abaye's mention of residents.
09.summary: Rav Yosef said he had never heard a certain ruling of Shmuel about adjacent roofs. His student Abaye told him that he had taught it to them himself, and repeated it. Rav Yosef then remembered and corrected Abaye's version, explaining what he had really said.
09.missing: The forgetting is implied rather than told; most of the exchange is the content of the halakha.

10.event: In a good mood, Rava boasted that he was like ben Azzai ready to answer any question, and a Sage asked him how many apples are needed for an eiruv.
10.turn: Rava answered that one cannot make an eiruv with apples, and the Sage cited a mishna implying that one can.
10.summary: Rava, feeling sharp, declared himself like ben Azzai in the markets of Tiberias, ready for any question. One of the Sages tested him by asking how many apples make an eiruv. Rava replied that apples cannot be used, and the Sage challenged him from a mishna saying all foods combine for an eiruv.
10.missing: How Rava answered the challenge and how the exchange ended.

11.event: A ritual bath in Yavne presumed full was measured and found deficient, and Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva disputed the status of purifications done in it.
11.turn: After an exchange of parables, Rabbi Akiva produced an argument distinguishing the cases.
11.outcome: Rabbi Tarfon conceded, praising Akiva: whoever separates from you separates from life.
11.summary: A ritual bath in Yavne thought to hold the required amount was measured and found short. Rabbi Tarfon held that everything purified in it remained pure, while Rabbi Akiva held it impure, and they argued through parables about priests found disqualified. Rabbi Akiva showed that the bath's flaw was like a blemished priest's, and Rabbi Tarfon accepted it, telling Akiva that leaving him is like leaving life.

12.event: Rabbi Elazar ascended to Eretz Yisrael, was ordained, and was appointed to the council for intercalating the calendar.
12.turn: At each step he declared he had escaped one more of the curses Ezekiel pronounced on false prophets.
12.outcome: He had been spared all three curses.
12.summary: When Rabbi Elazar went up to the Land of Israel, he said he had escaped one curse. When he was ordained, he said two, and when he was seated on the calendar council, three. He was referring to Ezekiel's curse that false prophets would not enter the land, be written in Israel's register, or sit in God's council.

13.missing: Only a bare mention that Abaye and Rava disputed a balcony all their lives, cited as legal proof.

14.event: Rav came to Apsetaya and forbade its residents to climb even a stripped tree on Shabbat.
14.turn: He found the place lax in observance and added a protective stringency.
14.outcome: The stricter rule was imposed there.
14.summary: Rav visited Apsetaya and prohibited the people from climbing even a tree stripped of its branches on Shabbat. The Gemara explains that this was not the basic law: he found the place neglectful and built a fence around it.
14.missing: The episode is cited briefly as a legal precedent; no reaction or aftermath is told.

15.event: At his son's wedding Rava served drinks; two Sages stood for him and two did not.
15.turn: Rava became angry at those who did not stand.
15.outcome: He rebuked them, asking whether they alone were Sages and the others not.
15.summary: Rava poured drinks for the guests at his son's wedding. Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua stood when he approached, but Rav Mari and Rav Pinehas son of Rav Hisda did not. Rava was offended and asked sharply whether those two thought themselves Sages and the others not.

16.actor: Mar Yehuda, Rav Yosef and Rav Shmuel son of Rabba bar bar Hana, and Rabba
16.event: Mar Yehuda found the two scholars at the door of Rabba's study hall and posed a contradiction between two baraitot about Rabbi Shimon.
16.turn: They were silent and had no answer, so they went to Rabba.
16.outcome: Rabba told them a quarrelsome person had put them up to it and resolved the contradiction.
16.summary: Mar Yehuda met Rav Yosef and Rav Shmuel son of Rabba bar bar Hana at the entrance to Rabba's study hall and challenged them with two seemingly contradictory teachings of Rabbi Shimon. They could not answer and fell silent. They brought the question to Rabba, who said an argumentative person had set them up and explained that one teaching dealt with an animal found to be a tereifa.

17.event: Rabbi Zeira avoided his teacher Rav Yehuda because he wanted to move to Eretz Yisrael and Rav Yehuda held that doing so violated a commandment.
17.summary: Rabbi Zeira wanted to go up to the Land of Israel, but his teacher Rav Yehuda taught that leaving Babylonia for Israel transgresses a commandment. So Rabbi Zeira kept out of his teacher's sight.
17.missing: What happened next: whether he left, met Rav Yehuda, or how it ended.

18.event: Rabbi Hanina regularly sent four dinars to a pauper each Shabbat eve; one day he sent them with his wife.
18.turn: She came back saying the man did not need charity, having overheard his household asked whether he dined on silver or gold tablecloths.
18.outcome: Rabbi Hanina responded by quoting Rabbi Elazar that we should be grateful to swindlers, since they excuse our failures toward the truly poor.
18.summary: Rabbi Hanina used to send a poor man four dinars every Friday. Once he sent his wife with the money, and she returned saying the man did not need it: she had heard people in his house asking whether he would dine on silver or gold tablecloths. Rabbi Hanina answered with Rabbi Elazar's saying that we should thank the swindlers, because without them we would be sinning every day by neglecting the poor.

19.actor: A man from Shot Mishot and Rabbi Yitzhak Nappaha
19.event: A man told the Sages he came from Shot Mishot, and Rabbi Yitzhak Nappaha stood and declared that the place lies between the rivers.
19.turn: The declaration implied the man's lineage was as sound as that of the exile community.
19.summary: A man told the Sages he was from Shot Mishot. Rabbi Yitzhak Nappaha rose and announced that Shot Mishot is between the rivers, a region whose families count as having good lineage.
19.missing: The text moves into legal geography; it does not say what became of the man.

20.event: Rabbi Akiva picked an etrog on the first of Shevat and separated two tithes from it.
20.turn: He tithed it according to both Beit Shammai's and Beit Hillel's dating of the new year for trees.
20.summary: Rabbi Akiva picked an etrog on the first of Shevat. Unsure which year's tithing rules applied, he separated two tithes, one according to Beit Shammai and one according to Beit Hillel.
20.missing: A single act cited as legal proof; no turn or consequence is told.
